text:
jia: Heads up — while running the quantization eval batch this morning I noticed a bunch of traces in S3 with truncated `model_output` fields. looks like the runner is dropping long responses when artifact size exceeds ~128KB. anyone seen this?

alex_m: ugh. do you have an example key or path?

jia: s3://redwood-evals/quant-run/2026-03-20/trace-0031.jsonl.gz => last entry ends mid-sentence. grabbed local log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-20T09:12:11Z runner: upload failed, err=object too large, status=413
2026-03-20T09:12:11Z trace: shard=7 sample_id=abc123 partial=true
```

maria: 413 from S3? usually that's proxy/nginx or our upload lambda choking. infra-bot, any recent changes to multipart policy? :eyes: 

infra-bot: Upload gateway patched 2026-03-19 04:07 UTC. Max request body changed from 200KB to 128KB to protect against syscall spikes. See infra#2147.

sam_w: that policy is too small for quant experiments. quantized outputs + per-token logits + metadata easily exceed 128KB for long dialogs. We either chunk traces or switch to compressed column storage.

leo: +1 on chunking. propose: split `model_output` into `output_chunks` array with incremental indices, and keep a single metadata record. also recommend storing heavy token-level arrays as separate parquet blobs referenced by trace id. low-latency index is just the jsonl trace, large arrays in parquet.

alex_m: implementation detail: runner currently emits a single JSON blob per sample. I can change serializer to stream chunked multipart uploads with `x-amz-chunked` or fall back to S3 multipart. but we need schema changes so eval consumers don't break.

maria: schema change requires migration plan: - backward-compatible fields for 3 months - update eval dashboard ingesters - CI tests for both legacy and chunked traces - data-retention policy update (how long to keep full token logs?)

jia: For retention: suggest default 30 days for full token traces, 1 year for minimal metadata + scalar metrics. longer retention behind an opt-in (enterprise customers might want 90d). also need PII stripping before writing.

sam_w: +1 on PII. We should apply a mask step in the runner: run `pii-mask` plugin that replaces any detected email/creditcard/ssn patterns in `decoded_text` and also strip user IDs. Keep a hashed user_key instead.

leo: also, cost: storing token arrays uncompressed is expensive. Use snappy parquet with int16/uint8 encodings for token ids, and gzip for jsonl. approximate savings ~6x. I'll run numbers.

alex_m: plan of action from my side: 1) PR to change serializer to chunked multipart + emit `output_chunks` field (backcompat: keep `model_output_raw` until cutover) 2) add S3 multipart retries and 413 handling 3) add unit test that simulates gateway 413 and verifies chunk fallback

maria: CI wiring: we need a new integration test in `eval-runner-e2e` that runs with `MAX_BODY=64KB` to exercise chunking and ensure dashboard ingestion handles both formats. also add a lint rule in `schema/` to validate presence of `trace_version` and `chunked=true/false`.

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-2368 "Eval runner: chunked trace upload + retention defaults" (assignee: alex_m)

jia: thanks. one more ask: can we add sampling controls so we don't capture full token traces for every sample? maybe a deterministic sampler: 1% full-token, 100% metadata. helps with budget and gives us reproducible coverage.

sam_w: yes — deterministic by hash of sample_id and rollout seed. Also add a `trace_sample_reason` field (e.g., "error", "regression", "sampled") so downstream dashboards can filter.

leo: and put an LRU cache on the runner to keep partial token arrays on disk until multipart finishes. prevents re-encoding thrash.

alex_m: I'll start the serializer PR today. will mock the new schema in the local ingest pipeline so we can iterate quickly.

maria: thanks all. can we review the PR Thurs 10am? I'll invite platform and dashboards.

jia: Thursday works. tagging followups: @alex_m (serializer), @leo (storage format), @sam_w (sampling + costs), @maria (CI + schema). :thumbsup:
